transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Ariela Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood Solutions Eng), Raj Patel (CTO, HelixCare), Sofia Lopez (Head of ML), Tom Becker (Infra Eng), Mina Yu (Security)

Summary: Technical deep dive to walk through OpenTelemetry integration for token-level metrics, how Redwood emits spans/metrics for runtime events (batching, KV cache hits/misses, quantization flags), recommended OTEL collector config for on-prem/VPC, and example dashboards and alerts. Customer caring about privacy/egress, sampling strategy, and tail-latency troubleshooting.

Topics: OpenTelemetry (OTLP) export, token-level per-token metrics, span design (request vs token spans), KV cache visibility, batching and sequence length effects, quantization indicators in traces, exporter and collector placement in VPC/on-prem, Grafana dashboards and SLOs, cost/latency tradeoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00:10] Ariela Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll go through the tracing/metrics story end to end; Maya and Ethan from infra and runtime will cover the instrumentations and examples, we'll leave time for Qs, uh, at the end.
[00:00:25] Raj Patel: thanks, quick note, we have Mina from security, Tom from infra and Sofia from ML, we're mainly trying to prove we can get token-level visibility without sending PII off-prem, also want to see tail-latency and cache effectiveness.
[00:00:40] Maya Singh: great, yep, goal is: how do we get per-request and per-token metrics into HelixCare's observability stack, whether that's an internal OTEL collector or an agent you host in VPC. we'll sketch spans and metrics.
[00:01:08] Ethan Cole: just to set context, Redwood emits a mix of metrics + traces. metrics for counters/hists like token_count, latency_ms, batch_size, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses; traces for request lifecycle and optional token spans for very fine grained troubleshooting.
[00:01:33] Tom Becker: quick Q, how much data are we talking if you enable token-level spans for production? our egress is limited.
[00:01:45] Maya Singh: yeah that's a big one. token-level spans are high-cardinality. we recommend adaptive sampling: capture token spans for, say, 1% of requests and always capture the edge cases (errors, >99th tail). also emit aggregated metrics per request: token_rate, median_token_latency, token_histogram so you don't need every span for dashboards.
[00:02:10] Sofia Lopez: when you say aggregated metrics per request, is that a histogram per model? per route? we need to split by model_variant and quantization profile.
[00:02:25] Ethan Cole: yes per-route and per-model tags: model_name, model_variant, quantized=true|false, seq_len_bucket, and environment (prod/stage). we use attributes on spans and labels on metrics. e.g., histogram: redwood.request.tokens.latency_ms with labels model_variant and batch_size.
[00:02:55] Mina Yu: we cannot send any user-generated content out. what's the redwood recommendation for redacting prompts or disabling payload export?
[00:03:10] Maya Singh: good catch. we never export raw prompt text by default in telemetry. we send metadata-only attributes: token_count, classes of error, anonymized request_id; raw tokens are never sent unless you explicitly enable "debug capture" and opt-in. for on-prem you can keep collector internal, no egress.
[00:03:37] Raj Patel: ok that helps. show us the span model.
[00:03:45] Maya Singh: sure. top-level span: redwood.request (duration = full response time). children: redwood.kv_cache.lookup (tags: hit|miss, key_size, kv_latency_ms), redwood.batch.dispatch (batch_size, batched=true), redwood.token.emit spans (optional, token_index, token_latency_ms, is_cached_token). token spans are optional and sampled.
[00:04:20] [00:04:35] Ethan Cole: one thing we do in the runtime is annotate spans with quantization_profile so you can compare 4-bit vs 8-bit throughput/latency. that helps when you experiment with quantization.
[00:04:58] Tom Becker: about KV cache keys - are those hashed or raw? we need to avoid PII in keys.
[00:05:12] Maya Singh: keys are hashed and truncated by default; we also expose only hit/miss and cache_hit_rate metrics, no raw prefix. you can also configure TTL and eviction metrics.
[00:05:38] Raj Patel: instrumentation: what's required on our side? install collector? endpoint?
[00:05:48] Ariela Chen: three options: 1) Hosted OTLP: Redwood exports to a managed endpoint (not an option for you right now). 2) Private VPC: you run an OTEL collector in your VPC pointing to your internal backends (Prometheus / Grafana / Splunk). 3) On-prem: same collector but air-gapped, we provide sample config and container images. we generally recommend the collector as sidecar or a dedicated daemon set.
[00:06:21] Tom Becker: how do you suggest we handle Prometheus metrics vs traces?
[00:06:30] Ethan Cole: metrics (prom counters/hists) are best for SLOs and alerting. traces are for tracing specific requests and debugging. we export OTLP -> collector -> metrics backend and traces optionally to Jaeger/Tempo. we also provide a Grafana dashboard that consumes Prometheus metrics + Tempo for trace links.
[00:06:58] Sofia Lopez: can you show example dashboard panels for tail latency and cache efficiency?
[00:07:07] Maya Singh: yep, slide deck has panel examples: P95/P99 latency by model_variant, token latency histogram (buckets), cache_hit_rate over time, batch size distribution, quantization comparison panel (latency vs tokens/sec). we'll share the JSON.
[00:07:30] Raj Patel: what about token-level metrics tied to cost - can we get per-token cost estimates?
[00:07:40] Ethan Cole: we emit token_count and tokens_generated per request, you can multiply by your unit cost. for Redwood Dedicated we can approximate GPU token cost per model variant; we'll provide a cost-per-token baseline in the pilot.
[00:07:58] [00:08:15] Mina Yu: sampling policy question: do you support dynamic sampling, like increase sample rate on errors or high tail?
[00:08:22] Maya Singh: yes dynamic/adaptive sampling. you can configure collector rules: sample if response code != 200, if latency > threshold, or if kv_cache_miss rate > X. that way you capture problematic flows.
[00:08:45] Tom Becker: slightly worried about cardinality from model_variant tags - we have many model versions. any suggestions?
[00:08:56] Ethan Cole: we recommend a model_version alias strategy: expose model_family + alias_tag, avoid raw git/shas. rollups and relabeling in the collector help reduce cardinality.
[00:09:20] Raj Patel: demonstration please, Maya?
[00:09:26] Maya Singh: sure, walk through a synthetic request. [screen share noises] so request starts, redwood.request span starts: attributes: request_id=abc123, model=rw-large, quantized=4bit, seq_len=128. batch_size=4. first child: kv_cache.lookup: label hit=false, latency 2.6ms. next child: batch.dispatch duration ~12ms, then token emits (sampled) token_index 0 latency 6ms...
[00:10:05] [00:10:20] Ethan Cole: you can see the token spans link to the cache lookup via attributes is_cached_token=true/false. in Grafana we link traces to the Prometheus panel that shows cache_hit_rate.
[00:10:40] Sofia Lopez: for our evals we need to compare quantization quality vs token latency. can the traces include a quality score attribute?
[00:10:52] Maya Singh: yes you can include an eval_score attribute at request closure; it's an integer or float aggregated as a metric. we usually output redwood.request.quality_score. remember not to include message text.
[00:11:18] Tom Becker: operationally - how much CPU/memory does the instrumentation add on the inference host?
[00:11:26] Ethan Cole: minimal for metrics; token spans add overhead if you enable them. for example token spans at 1% sample rate add ~5-8% CPU overhead in our bench; aggregated metrics are <1% CPU. numbers vary by model/resolution and quantization.
[00:11:52] Raj Patel: your bench numbers - are they on GPU? what instance types?
[00:11:59] Maya Singh: our perf runs are on A100/RTX8000 equiv. we include a hardware matrix in the doc. for CPU overhead on the CPU side it's small; main cost is network if you send raw spans externally.
[00:12:20] Mina Yu: on-prem constraints: we need collector within our air-gapped network. will Redwood support an installer?
[00:12:30] Ariela Chen: yes we have an on-prem package: container images and Helm charts for the OTEL collector + Redwood-provided dashboard JSON. we also provide a support bundle generator that creates sanitized capture for debug which you can vet before sending.
[00:12:52] Tom Becker: what about encryption and KMS for logs/metrics?
[00:12:57] Maya Singh: we support TLS for OTLP, mTLS for collector endpoints, and you can configure KMS for S3 buckets if you forward metrics/logs to object storage. for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
[00:13:18] [00:13:40] Raj Patel: let's talk about alerts. suggested SLOs?
[00:13:46] Ethan Cole: recommended SLOs: request latency P95 < 250ms for short responses, P99 < 800ms, kv_cache_hit_rate > 85% for prefix-based workloads. alert on rising tail or drop in cache_hit_rate or increase in batch_size variance.
[00:14:10] Sofia Lopez: batch_size variance? what do you mean?
[00:14:15] Maya Singh: if your batch size spikes unexpectedly it could indicate a backlog or queuing; create a panel for avg batch size and alert if avg_batch_size > configured threshold or if batch wait time increases.
[00:14:41] Raj Patel: quantization panel - show examples?
[00:14:48] Maya Singh: we have a compare panel: latency vs tokens/sec, with curves for 8bit vs 4bit; also quality_score difference boxplot. we'll share.
[00:15:05] Mina Yu: are any of these third-party libraries that pull data externally? open-telemetry is OSS but we run an internal collector.
[00:15:15] Ethan Cole: OTEL is OSS. the only outbound is to whichever backend you configure. for air-gapped, you keep collector internal, no outbound. Redwood's hosted telemetry would be outbound but disabled by default for private deployments.
[00:15:40] Raj Patel: ok, let's dig into a failure mode: sudden P99 spike and cache miss increase. what traces do we look for?
[00:15:48] Maya Singh: start with the cache_hit_rate metric, then look at traces of redwood.request where kv_cache.lookup shows miss and kv_latency spikes. token spans can show if token_emit latency increases after a miss. sampling policy should ensure we have traces for errors.
[00:16:12] Ethan Cole: also check batch.dispatch duration and batch queue length - a slow downstream or crowded GPU can increase dispatch time, so batch_size and seq_len distribution panels help.
[00:16:30] [00:16:45] Sofia Lopez: do you expose internal runtime counters like kv_index_size or cache_evictions?
[00:16:52] Maya Singh: yes metrics: kv_index_size, kv_evictions_total, kv_ttl_seconds, kv_hit_rate_percent. key sizes are hashed so no raw keys.
[00:17:08] Tom Becker: what about integrating with our existing tracing pipeline - we run an internal OTEL collector chain that forwards to Splunk. any compatibility issues?
[00:17:18] Ariela Chen: none, OTLP gRPC and OTLP/HTTP are supported. we provide example relabel configs and resource attributes so you can join Redwood traces with your app traces.
[00:17:36] Raj Patel: curious about retention - how long should we keep token-level traces?
[00:17:44] Ethan Cole: token-level traces are heavy; retain sampled traces longer for PIIs we can't store. typical pattern: keep aggregates for 90d, full sampled traces for 14d, and extend on-demand. depends on storage policy.
[00:18:05] Mina Yu: any regulatory considerations for EU data residency?
[00:18:12] Maya Singh: for hosted we can pin regions; for Private/Dedicated you control collector endpoints and storage locations. we can support EU-only storage for metrics/logs.
[00:18:30] [00:18:45] Raj Patel: Can we see a concrete OTEL collector config?
[00:18:51] Maya Singh: yes we'll send a couple. default: receivers: otlp; processors: batch, resource; exporters: prometheusremotewrite or otlp; service pipelines for metrics and traces; relabeling to drop high-card tags. we include relabel examples to squash model_version into model_family alias.
[00:19:20] Tom Becker: any gotchas with Prometheus histograms for token latency?
[00:19:27] Ethan Cole: pick buckets thoughtfully - token latency can be 0.1ms to 200ms; too many buckets increases cardinality. use logarithmic buckets and aggregate at request level for dashboards.
[00:19:46] Sofia Lopez: how do you tie model evals back to production traces for quality regression?
[00:19:55] Maya Singh: add an eval_id attribute on the request and produce redwood.request.quality_score metric; then you can compare panels across eval_id. also use canary labels for rollouts.
[00:20:18] Raj Patel: what's the recommended rollout for enabling token-level spans in prod?
[00:20:25] Ethan Cole: 1) enable aggregated metrics only; 2) enable token spans at very low sample (0.1-1%); 3) add dynamic rules for errors and tail; 4) increase sampling in canary.
[00:20:43] Mina Yu: what about encryption of OTLP traffic?
[00:20:47] Maya Singh: OTLP supports TLS; we recommend mTLS for collector endpoints. we provide examples for cert management with Vault or KMS.
[00:21:10] [00:21:30] Ariela Chen: quick pause - any other questions before we go into the demo artifacts?
[00:21:35] Raj Patel: one more - how much of the telemetry is configurable at per-tenant level?
[00:21:41] Ethan Cole: everything is configurable per-tenant: sampling, which spans emitted, attributes redaction, and exporter endpoints. for Dedicated we can also keep telemetry isolated per customer.
[00:22:05] Maya Singh: demo artifacts now: share Grafana panels, a small sample OTEL collector yaml, and an example relabel config.
[00:22:18] [screen share noises for a demo of dashboard and trace links]
[00:22:40] Maya Singh: here is the sample Grafana panel: P95 latency by model_variant split, P99 table, cache_hit_rate over time, token_latency_histogram. trace links in the panel open Tempo with the sampled redwood.request trace.
[00:23:05] Sofia Lopez: do you have a CSV or sample data we can run?
[00:23:11] Ethan Cole: yes we'll include synthetic workload generator and a sequence length distribution file; that'll let you reproduce our dashboards locally.
[00:23:30] Raj Patel: ok let's map next steps - we want the sample configs, pilot kickoff and security review.
[00:23:40] Ariela Chen: noted - we'll send the artifact bundle and schedule pilot kickoff once you share the workload.
[00:23:52] [00:24:05] Mina Yu: security follow-up: we need a design for on-prem collector auth and a proof that no message text leaves our network.
[00:24:12] Maya Singh: we'll produce a security note + support bundle guide that shows how we sanitize captures.
[00:24:30] Raj Patel: thanks, this was helpful. any final quick tips?
[00:24:36] Ethan Cole: start with metrics, keep token spans sampled, use relabeling to manage cardinality, and track cache_hit_rate as your leading indicator.
[00:24:50] Ariela Chen: thanks everyone, we'll send the dashboard JSON and OTEL yaml after the call and cc Mina for the security notes.
